canary-server.name: canary-server
canary-server.description: Use this skill to get canary work done through a workspace's request server, including from places canary is not installed: the workspace's carl (.canary/share/carl, curl-like, needs only sh) or the inbox files directly.
canary-server.body:
# Canary request server: driving canary without canary

## What this skill is for

Use it when canary work should be done through a workspace's request server: the work
must run on another machine, queue behind other work, or you are somewhere canary is
not installed. You need only a POSIX shell and the shared filesystem. No canary, no
Python.

## First actions

```sh
WS=/path/to/workspace                 # the directory holding .canary
CARL=$WS/.canary/share/carl           # installed by `canary server start`
URL=file://$WS
$CARL GET $URL/server                 # 'state': 'running'; exit 7 = no server
$CARL POST $URL/canary/help -s        # every route, what it does and its fields
$CARL POST $URL/canary/schema -s      # the JSON schema of every body
```

The other skills say `canary query -c TOPIC` or `canary learn skills SKILL`. Here you
get the same data from `/canary/learn/*`; see "The CLI, as routes" below.

If `carl` or `server.json` is missing, no server has run here: someone with canary
starts one on the machine that should do the work (`canary server start`, after loading
the modules the tests need). You cannot start it without canary.

## Run, read, cancel

```sh
$CARL POST $URL/canary/run -d '{"pathspec": ["tests"], "only": "all"}'   # waits, prints result.json
$CARL POST $URL/canary/status -s                                        # latest result of every job
$CARL POST $URL/canary/query/failures -s                                # the latest session's failures
$CARL POST $URL/canary/run -d '{"only": "failed"}' -H 'Idempotency-Key: rerun-1' -m 3600
$CARL GET  $URL/requests/rerun-1                                        # its result, or its status
$CARL POST $URL/requests/rerun-1/cancel                                 # or Ctrl-C while carl waits
```

- The result: `state` done | rejected | cancelled | failed, `status_code` 200 |
  400/404/409 | 499 | 500, `data`, `error`. For work, read `data.exit_code`: canary's
  exit code. 0 means all passed and 7 means nothing ran. Otherwise it is a sum of bits,
  one per kind of job that did not pass: 2 diffed, 4 timed out, 8 failed, 16 cancelled
  (e.g. never started), 32 did not finish, 64 another status. 1 and 3 mean canary itself
  failed. Read `error` and the request's `stderr` (`/canary/help` lists these as
  `exit_codes`).
- `data.pass_with_errors: N`: N jobs passed but a hook after them failed. They count as
  passes, so the exit code doesn't show them; `/canary/query/failures` lists them.
- `data.session_error` means canary itself crashed while it ran the session (e.g.
  `RuntimeError: ...`): its jobs show as cancelled or unfinished, but none of them is to
  blame. The traceback is in the request's `stderr`.
- `--cwd DIR` (relative to the workspace) and `--env NAME=VALUE` set where and with what
  the request runs. **Send only relative paths.** Paths in the body (`pathspec`, `roots`,
  `targets`) are relative to `--cwd`. The server may mount the workspace at a
  different path than you do, so it can't resolve your absolute paths.
- A `canaryhooks.py` in `--cwd` loads for the request. Its stderr says `Using hooks from
  .../canaryhooks.py (canaryhooks)`, and one that fails to import fails the request (500,
  with the import error).
- `-f` makes an error result exit 22; `-m SECONDS` stops waiting (exit 28; the request goes
  on: `GET` it later). carl's exit codes: 0 a result arrived, 2 usage, 6 no workspace in
  the URL, 7 no server, 130 cancelled.

## Routes

Work (one at a time, in arrival order): `/canary/run`, `/canary/hpc/run`,
`/canary/collect`, `/canary/select`, `/canary/rebaseline`.
`/canary/collect` checks generation only: it expands each file's directives but runs no
test body.
Reads (answer at once, even while work runs): `/canary/status`,
`/canary/query/{jobs,failures,sessions}`, `/canary/query/job/ID[/...]`,
`/canary/query/db`, `/canary/query/db/{schema,stats}`,
`/canary/query/session/NAME[/...]`, `/canary/location/ID`, `/canary/learn/{capabilities,skills}`, `/canary/help`,
`/canary/schema`.

- `/canary/query/job/ID` is everything about the job's latest run: its record (status,
  timings, `measurements`), its `spec` (parameters, keywords, command), `dependencies`,
  `variables`, `allocation`. `{"session_id": "S"}` picks its run in session S. Add
  segments to get part of it: `.../job/ID/measurements/loss`, `.../job/ID/spec/parameters`,
  `.../job/ID/env` (the run's environment). A missing key is a 404 that lists the keys there.
- `/canary/query/session/NAME` (`latest` works) is the session's `outcome_counts`, how it
  ran (`argv`, `returncode`, `started_on`, ...) and every job's record (`jobs`);
  `.../session/latest/jobs/0/measurements` goes deeper.
- `/canary/query/failures` lists the jobs that need attention: failed or aborted, and
  `PASS_WITH_ERRORS` (the test passed but a `canary_runtest_finish` hook raised; the
  reason says what). `{"log_tail": 20}` adds each one's last 20 lines of output: usually
  enough to see why, in one request.
- `/canary/query/job/ID/log` is what the job printed (`{"tail": 50}` for the end,
  `"stream": "stderr"` if it split stderr off): read it to see why a job failed.
  `/canary/location/ID` says where its files are, relative to the workspace: `exec_dir`,
  `log`, `input`, `source_dir`.
- Every job record (status, jobs, failures, a session's jobs) has `measurements`: name to
  value, as `add_measurement` recorded them.
- Reach for SQL last: the routes above answer most questions. `/canary/query/db` takes
  one `SELECT` (`{"sql": "... WHERE spec_name = ?", "params": ["x"]}`), at most 10 000
  rows; `"parse_json": true` returns JSON columns (`measurements`, `timekeeper`,
  `specs.data`) as objects. `PRAGMA` is refused: `/canary/query/db/schema` lists the
  tables and their columns (`.../schema/results/columns`), `/canary/query/db/stats`
  counts specs, results and sessions.

## The CLI, as routes

Commands in the other skills map to routes. Send the body with `-d`; reads may use `GET`.

| canary command | route | body |
|---|---|---|
| `canary run PATH ...` | `/canary/run` | `{"pathspec": ["PATH"]}` |
| `canary status` | `/canary/status` | |
| `canary query failures` | `/canary/query/failures` | |
| `canary query jobs --session S` | `/canary/query/jobs` | `{"session_id": "S"}` |
| `canary query job ID [A.B]` | `/canary/query/job/ID[/A/B]` | |
| `canary query session S [A.B]` | `/canary/query/session/S[/A/B]` | |
| `canary query sessions` | `/canary/query/sessions` | |
| `canary location ID` (`-x`, `-l`, `-i`, `-s`) | `/canary/location/ID` | |
| `canary log ID --tail N` (`-e` for stderr) | `/canary/query/job/ID/log` | `{"tail": N}` (`"stream": "stderr"`) |
| `canary query db "SELECT ..."` | `/canary/query/db` | `{"sql": "SELECT ..."}` |
| `canary query db schema`, `canary query db stats` | `/canary/query/db/schema`, `/canary/query/db/stats` | |
| `canary query -c TOPIC`, `canary learn capabilities TOPIC` | `/canary/learn/capabilities` | `{"topic": "TOPIC"}` |
| `canary query --skills SKILL`, `canary learn skills SKILL` | `/canary/learn/skills` | `{"topic": "SKILL"}` |
| `... --list` (learn) | the same route | add `"list_keys": true` |

```sh
$CARL GET $URL/canary/learn/capabilities -s -d '{"topic": "ext.pyt.parameters"}'
$CARL GET $URL/canary/learn/skills -s -d '{"topic": ".", "list_keys": true}'
```

A query path's dots are the route's segments: `canary query job ID measurements.loss` is
`/canary/query/job/ID/measurements/loss`. `/canary/help` lists each route's fields.
The routes do not cover every command yet.

## Without carl: the files

```sh
S=$WS/.canary/var/server
printf '%s\n' '{"path": "/canary/run", "request": {"pathspec": ["tests"]}}' > $S/inbox/r1.json.tmp
mv $S/inbox/r1.json.tmp $S/inbox/r1.json                  # the id is the file name
until [ -f $S/requests/r1/result.json ]; do sleep 1; done; cat $S/requests/r1/result.json
touch $S/requests/r1/cancel                               # cancel
```

Envelope keys: `version` (1), `path`, `request`, `cwd` (relative, default "."), `env`.
Anything else is rejected with 400. Output while a run goes is in `$S/requests/<id>/stdout`.

## Common mistakes

- Writing `inbox/<id>.json` directly instead of `.tmp`, then `mv`: half-written files.
- Reusing an id: 409, the request never runs; carl generates fresh ids.
- Reading only `state`: a run with failing tests is still `done`; check `data.exit_code`.
- Expecting your environment to apply: work runs in the server's (add `--env`).
- An absolute or `..` `--cwd`: rejected; it is relative to the workspace.
- An absolute path in the body, e.g. `{"pathspec": ["/home/me/ws/tests"]}`: the server
  looks for it on its own machine. If the path doesn't exist there, you get `400 ...: no
  such file or directory`; if it is outside the workspace, `403`. Send `tests`, relative
  to `--cwd`, instead. A tree outside the workspace is reachable only if the operator lists
  it in `server:allowed_roots`; results then show it as `name:path`.
- Expecting `canary rm` or `canary run -w` to work while a server (or any run) uses the
  workspace: refused; stop the server first.
